title: The Potter’s Gentle Hands
old_p1: Heavenly Father had something to show Jeremiah. 'Go down to the potter's house,' He said, 'and there I will speak to you.'
So Jeremiah went. The potter's wheel turned round and round, and wet clay rose up under two steady hands.
One pot did not come out right. It leaned and slumped and lost its shape right there in the potter's hands.
old_p2: The potter did not throw the clay away. He gathered it up and made it again into another good vessel, just as it seemed good to him.
'As the clay is in the potter's hand, so are ye in mine hand,' said Heavenly Father. You are in kind, patient hands tonight, being made into something lovely.
p1: Heavenly Father had something to show Jeremiah. “Go down to the potter’s house,” He said, “and I will talk to you there.” A potter makes pots and bowls out of soft, wet clay.
So Jeremiah went. The potter’s wheel turned round and round, and the wet clay rose up under the potter’s two steady hands.
One pot did not come out right. It leaned and flopped and lost its shape right there in the potter’s hands.
p2: The potter did not throw the clay away. He gathered it up and made it again into a good pot, just the way he wanted it.

“You are like the clay in the potter’s hand,” Heavenly Father said, “and I am like the potter.” When you make a mistake, Heavenly Father does not throw you away. He helps you start again. You are in kind, patient hands tonight.

stone_name: That safe, not-thrown-away feeling is called hopeful. Your mind might think, “I can try again.” Your body might feel lighter, with your shoulders coming back up.
